page: Microsoft Azure M128s_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance within the MSMediumMemoryv2 family. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor using an x86_64 Intel processor platform. The hardware configuration provides 128 dedicated virtual CPUs with no graphical processing units.

The server delivers 2048.0 GB of total RAM, yielding an allocation of 16.0 GB of system memory per vCPU. Local disk storage is not included, requiring persistent workloads to utilize external storage options such as Premium Storage. Network allocation includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Hardware resource allocation is designed for high memory density. Consolidating multi-terabyte datasets into a single compute node reduces the architectural complexity of distributed clusters, though storage costs depend entirely on external volume provisioning due to the lack of local drives. The instance is suited for large-scale enterprise databases, SAP HANA, extensive in-memory caches, and high-volume analytics workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure M128s_v2 is an enterprise-scale memory-optimized virtual machine from the MSMediumMemoryv2 series. Governed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance runs on an x86_64 Intel architecture equipped with 128 dedicated vCPUs. The primary distinguishing characteristic of the M128s_v2 is its memory capacity, providing 2048.0 GB of total system memory, which equates to a high density of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, relying on Premium Storage capabilities for persistent block storage needs. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. From a workload perspective, the substantial memory footprint and dedicated compute configuration make this instance suited for large in-memory databases, real-time enterprise analytics, relational database engines with multi-terabyte caches, and massive online transaction processing systems requiring high memory capacity within a single virtual machine boundary.
